matches.rationale: GT1 describes artificially inflated AC-ViT noise robustness margins in Table 2. Pred 6 explicitly states Table 2 values were 'adjusted to exaggerate AC-ViT's advantage,' and pred 14 notes that the conclusion’s claims of noise robustness are unsupported because they rely on that manipulated table. Both capture the same underlying data-integrity issue.

GT2 highlights logical flaws in the gradient decomposition of Section 2.2, including path count contradictions and ambiguous DG/NG definitions. Pred 2 finds a clear path-count error (127 vs 1024) in the same section’s worked example, and pred 5 identifies that the direct gradient is misattributed to Direct Feedback Alignment, which conflates the DG concept. Both issues fall under the same method-logic inconsistency.

GT3 concerns unequal training epochs for AC-ViT versus Residual ViT (700 vs 300). No finding addresses this ViT-specific discrepancy; pred 8 identifies a Mixer epoch mismatch in the same section, but that is a different architecture and a separate corruption.

GT4 concerns an overgeneralized universal claim in the Conclusion. None of the findings identify overbroad conclusions about matching baselines across all tasks. Pred 14 discusses the unsupported noise-robustness claim due to manipulated data, which is a data-integrity issue rather than an overgeneralization.

GT5 describes fabricated references and missing prior work in the Related Work section. Pred 12 finds an incorrect citation in Appendix G, but that is a different location and a different set of references, so it does not capture the same scientific issue.

GT6 flags the omission of environmental/energy implications of longer training. Pred 11 notes missing compute-resource details in the checklist, but it does not discuss environmental impact or sustainability, which is the core ethical omission.

GT7 points out that the Abstract’s ‘up to 18% reduction in catastrophic forgetting’ claim is presented as universal despite being qualified by specific configurations later. No finding discusses this forgetting-claim mismatch between Abstract and Section 6.
GT8 targets overly promotional language and inflated rhetoric in the Introduction. None of the findings identify such language manipulation in the Introduction.

GT9 states that Figure 6’s loss curves were manipulated to exaggerate AC-Mixer’s low-data advantage. Pred 7 explicitly notes the Figure 6 caption says the Residual Mixer test loss was ‘obscured to appear less converged, artificially enhancing AC-Mixer's relative performance,’ directly matching the plot manipulation.

GT10 describes omitted hyperparameter details (learning rates, regularization, initialization) throughout Sections 4–5, undermining reproducibility. Pred 10 flags the same omission in Section 4.2.1 and the false reproducibility claims in the checklist, capturing the identical incomplete-experimental-protocol issue.

GT11 warns that the up-to-18% forgetting reduction claim on Split CIFAR-100 is overstated as general continual-learning superiority. No finding addresses this specific overclaim or its narrow benchmark scope.
GT12 concerns promotional phrasing (‘remarkable success,’ ‘superior performance’) in the Abstract. None of the findings identify or criticize such rhetorical inflation in the Abstract.
GT13 flags the absence of fairness/bias impact discussion in the ethics statement. No finding mentions fairness, bias, or demographic impacts of architectural compression.

GT14 reports that baselines receive fewer epochs or smaller batch sizes, confounding comparisons; the corrupted text points to the MLP-Mixer experiment. Pred 8 directly reveals that the Residual Mixer was trained for 300 epochs while AC-Mixer received 420 epochs under a claim of identical compute budgets, which is the same unfair comparison issue.

GT15 asserts that Figures 2 and 3 present overly smooth, monotonic curves without error bars, masking variance. Pred 15 reports that the figures are entirely missing/unreadable placeholders; that is a different issue (absent evidence vs. manipulated visual presentation).

GT16 describes an inconsistency between the claimed linear backward-path count (L-i+1) and experimental gradient heatmaps showing more complex patterns. No finding addresses this theory–experiment gradient-flow contradiction.
